reviewer: Codex parent agent, direct image inspection
limitations: Contact-sheet inspection at 320 pixels per view, not full-resolution certification of all images.
Only 50 TRAIN windows were inspected; unseen windows may contain issues.
Broad skill intervals include preparation, carrying, retraction and settling; intent is not action completion.
Open/close commands do not establish physical contact, grasp success or final task success.
Exact native23 targets are not yet a validated executable VLM output protocol.
scope: Each listed case was visually inspected at t, t+8, t+16 in head, left-wrist and right-wrist views. Numerical labels are exact original native controls, not inferred from images. This is not a grasp/outcome or native-macro equivalence certificate.

cases.observation: Head scene rotates smoothly while both wrist views remain floor-facing; consistent with base yaw command. Radio is not visible here; NAVIGATE target is an instruction, not a visibility claim.

Radio beside the right hand at the coffee table, right wrist sees a close cropped red side; torso/right-arm adjustment and constant close command are retained. Occlusion does not establish grasp success.
Right hand approaches the radio with substantial image change, left hand also repositions; consistent with multi-arm GRASP approach, not a single LEFT motion.
Right wrist and hand reposition around the radio while the left/table view is comparatively stable; current and future views are continuous. No claim of completed grasp.

Right hand supports the radio and left hand approaches its front control area; both wrists change coherently with PRESS annotation and dual-arm command activity. Actual power state is not visually certified.
Left hand/radio near coffee-table surface; left fingers visibly open by the last view, consistent with recorded -1 to +1 gripper target during PLACEON. No release/stability success inferred.
Left hand supports radio while right hand aims toward its front; mixed dual-arm PRESS motion remains coherent across the three times. Close cropped radio in left wrist is expected occlusion.

Initial arms unfold from body-occluded wrist views while base command is zero under broad NAVIGATE instruction. This is startup/posture motion, not evidence of completed navigation; dark views are robot occlusion rather than missing frames.
Radio remains on table in head view; arms move out of body/floor-facing wrist views during GRASP preparation. Wrist-only target visibility is poor, but no scene or camera discontinuity is apparent.
cases.caveat: target absent or occluded in wrist views

cases.observation: Radio near table, right gripper command remains open while torso rises and both EEF positions shift together; consistent with a late PLACEON/retraction interval. Green front detail is not used as an official success label.
Room rotates smoothly under negative-yaw navigation while wrists face the floor and arm poses remain nearly fixed. No cross-camera scene mismatch apparent.
Robot moves through room toward floor cans while right hand carries the wastebasket; base plus small torso adjustment is visible, with stable carried geometry in right wrist.

Left-held orange soda can is positioned toward the right-held wastebasket; all three views are consistent with PLACEIN approach and modest left-arm motion. Release/success not inferred from closed grippers.
Right wrist approaches a wastebasket on the floor, with grippers open; fits GRASP preparation rather than a completed grasp. Scene and camera order remain continuous.

Left-held blue soda can descends toward wastebasket held by right hand; an orange can is already visible inside. Dual-arm command/PLACEIN instruction matches the sampled visual sequence without claiming final placement success.

Right wrist sees the floor wastebasket interior/rim and right fingers close between middle and final views, consistent with right gripper target +1 to -1 while arms are nearly fixed. No lift or holding success is established.

Small base/torso adjustment changes the approach to the floor wastebasket; right wrist looks into the bin and both grippers remain open. Smooth body positioning under GRASP instruction, not completed grasp.
Head scene rotates smoothly past refrigerator and dining table under positive-yaw navigation; arms remain quiet and wrists floor-facing. Wastebasket instruction does not claim current visibility.

Torso lowers both hands about five centimetres toward a blue soda can visible in the left wrist; right hand carries the basket with an orange can inside. Left gripper stays open during approach, not grasp completion.

Wastebasket with orange and blue cans remains on the floor while the open right hand withdraws slightly upward. Consistent with late PLACEON/retraction, without asserting official completion or required object count.

Head/floor scenery translates while a large round object remains close to the left wrist and the right hand adjusts slightly. Simultaneous lateral/forward base command is retained; close object occlusion is not a missing image.

Pumpkins remain close to both wrists while head scenery rotates and the torso raises both hands about four centimetres. Fits carrying during navigation, with no scene/camera discontinuity; constant close targets do not independently prove holding.

Right wrist sees the pale pillar-like object near the open cabinet while the open left hand and torso adjust. PLACEIN is a broad intent here; the sampled interval does not show release or completed placement.
Pumpkin remains on floor in head and right-wrist views as hands/torso approach downward with both grippers open. Consistent GRASP preparation, not a completed grasp or a closed-gripper label.

Hands and torso reposition at cabinet front under OPEN DRAWER instruction; wrist perspectives change smoothly and fingers stay open. Target_part=right describes the cabinet part, not proof that the right hand alone is acting; visible opening success is not inferred.

Pale pillar-like object is close to the right wrist over an open drawer containing other objects; right gripper target switches closed to open while arm motion is small. Visual continuity is good, but the occluded contact/release does not certify stable placement.

Both hands reposition at the open drawer front, with larger left than right displacement and open grippers. Drawer remains visibly open through this short CLOSE DRAWER interval; intent is not an outcome label.

Initial living-room head view and heavily occluded wrist views evolve continuously while arms start unfolding and a small yaw command appears. NAVIGATE cauldron is broad intent, not evidence that the black near-camera occluder is that target.
cases.caveat: startup wrist occlusion; no target identification

cases.observation: Small forward base command moves hands/cameras closer to the drawer front while joint poses are almost unchanged; wrist views become dominated by the wood face. Fits body-assisted CLOSE DRAWER approach; drawer is not certified fully closed.

Cabinet fronts appear closed while arms lower/retract and torso adjusts, with both grippers open. This late CLOSE DRAWER segment is post-action repositioning rather than continued drawer-contact motion; no official task success inferred.
cases.caveat: post-action motion within broad skill interval

cases.observation: Right hand supports a food plate at the open refrigerator while base yaw and small left-hand adjustment change head/floor geometry smoothly. Right wrist is heavily occluded by nearby fridge/plate geometry; head view supplies plate context. No successful insertion or stability guarantee inferred.
cases.caveat: right wrist target occlusion during placement

cases.observation: Hands approach bowls on the breakfast table with open grippers; torso lowers both EEF positions around one centimetre and left wrist sees a close white rim. Consistent with GRASP approach, not a release or completed grasp.
Left hand adjusts at a white bowl and fingers close as the target switches +1 to -1; right wrist remains floor/body-facing. Bowl rim occludes part of left view, and a completed lift is not shown.

Near stairs, torso/right-hand posture changes while base command is zero; wrists remain floor-facing. NAVIGATE fridge covers posture preparation, not a claim that fridge is currently visible or that this interval translates the base.

Both open hands approach the near food plate on the table while base advances slightly; head and both wrist views show coherent plate-edge motion. Food remains on the plate in sampled images, but no grasp/lift success is asserted.

Food plate is positioned at a fridge shelf while right hand lowers slightly and fingers visibly open, matching target -1 to +1. Head view retains plate context absent from the close side-on wrist view; this is release evidence, not official stable-placement success.

Robot advances/turns toward the still-closed refrigerator and raises the right hand during OPEN DOOR preparation. Wrist views remain floor/lower-door-facing and continuous; no door-open outcome is claimed.

Initial doorway head view stays nearly fixed as both arms unfold from close body-occluded wrist views; base command is zero. NAVIGATE fridge is a broad startup instruction, not visible fridge evidence.
cases.caveat: startup posture and severe wrist occlusion

cases.observation: Right-held food plate stays stable relative to the wrist while kitchen/head geometry changes during simultaneous base translation/yaw. Both arm poses are nearly fixed, so this is carried-object navigation, not pure isolated yaw or arm movement.

Bowls are visible in the sink while hands are down and largely quiet with open grippers. Late PLACEIN segment contains small settling/retraction rather than visible active placement; no completed-task truth derived from the endpoint.

Right-held hinged jar remains close to the right wrist while kitchen scenery rotates under negative base yaw; sausages appear on the nearby board in the head view. Fits navigation while carrying, with nearly fixed arms.

Base yaw plus torso/both-arm posture adjustment changes view of kitchen and upper cabinets smoothly; wrist views remain dominated by light floor/body geometry. Open grippers and NAVIGATE intent do not claim object holding.

Left hand approaches a hinged jar on an upper cabinet shelf while base translates/turns slightly; left-wrist jar view grows and shifts continuously, right wrist stays body-facing. Grippers remain open, so no completed grasp is inferred.

Left hand carries jar and right hand carries sausage while both arms reposition and base rotates toward placement. Coherent dual-object views demonstrate why one isolated-direction command would omit part of the expert action; insertion/release is not shown.
Left hand supports a lidded jar while right hand rises toward it, with slight base motion. OPEN LID is preparatory intent here; the jar remains visibly lidded and no open-lid outcome is claimed.

Right fingers close around a sausage on the cutting board while left hand carries a jar; right target switches +1 to -1 and arm poses are nearly fixed. Actual closure is visible but the interval does not establish a successful lift.

Left hand stays raised near an already-open upper cabinet door and repositions slightly; right wrist remains body-facing. Small coordinated motion within OPEN DOOR interval is continuous, without inferring which instant established opening.

Initial head view shows the kitchen island and sausage board while both arms unfold from body-occluded wrists; base command stays zero. NAVIGATE top cabinet is startup intent, not target visibility or completed navigation.
cases.caveat: startup posture and severe wrist occlusion

cases.observation: Right hand carries a jar at upper-cabinet height while base advances laterally/forward and arm poses remain almost fixed. Right wrist close-up and head shelf geometry evolve coherently; PLACEIN has not visibly released the jar.

Upper cabinet fronts appear closed as right hand retracts toward a body-facing wrist pose, with open grippers and stationary base. Late CLOSE DOOR includes retraction, not a new success label or continued contact requirement.
